summary: I audited the information architecture that turns the database into indexable pages, from the route files, the sitemap builder, the nav, the live site (Chrome UA) and the place tables (supabase-js, aggregated in JS). The live sitemap index serves five children totalling 9,292 URLs (core 205, geo 4,827, listings 3,283, matrix 885, content 92; 30 duplicates). geo.xml is 2,643 /subdivisions plat pages and 1,815 /homes-for-sale/{city}/{sub} browse pages plus 115 /zip, 61 /oregon; the 13 neighborhood pages (all Bend districts) sit in core.xml; no /types/ URL is in any sitemap. The listings sitemap is now 100% service-area (SITE-33 fixed). Verified defects, in order of damage to being seen: (1) the search-owned phrase '{City} homes for sale' was copied onto every place class by commit ffcc52e80 (2026-09-17, Node: none) and the seo-shell gate was rewritten to require it, so /cities/bend and /homes-for-sale/bend now carry identical title and H1 while PAGE_OUTLINE.md says the city page must own '{City} real estate'; (2) 59% of the browse-pair sitemap URLs have no active listing (DB: 1,919 pairs with >=3 lifetime, 782 with an active) and a live sample rendered 'No homes match this search right now' with index,follow on 9 of 12; (3) the 2,643 plat pages became sitemap-only orphans on 2026-09-18 when SITE-128 removed the city-page plat section, while the /subdivisions 'directory' lists 59 registry plats; (4) 651 subdivisions exist under both URL families with the same H1; (5) the sitemap submits 105 /zip URLs that 404 (route has dynamicParams=false over 10 ZIPs) plus a 308 (/luxury-homes-bend) and a 301 (/homes-for-sale/bend/awbrey-butte); (6) property-type pages are indexable but in no sitemap and no menu, community type pages have zero inbound links, and each competes with a sitemapped preset twin; (7) 454 indexable plats have had no sale in two years and render templated filler (bartel-addition: 10 sales, last 2020, zero active), and /subdivisions/blakley-heights returns 500; (8) subdivision_descriptions holds 0 rows, so no plat or browse page has a unique sentence; (9) 61 /oregon 'outside our market' pages (Portland, Salem, Eugene) are indexable after the cap was widened 25->100; (10) the header exposes no property types or neighborhoods and its Buy link is a ?view= URL; (11) lastmod is now() on 4,740 of 4,827 geo URLs; (12) place pages ship 1.7-3.8 MB of HTML. The exposure model has the right nouns (city, district, community, ZIP, plat, type) but publishes them as two overlapping URL families with no crawl path, no bar for emptiness, no bar for staleness, and no prose. What Google and AI engines cannot see is the depth: it exists in boundaries (3,427 plat polygons), subdivision_plat_closed_mv (2,642 plats with 10+ closes) and 13 well-written neighborhood rows, but it is reachable only through a sitemap. Three targeted row reads went through the MCP SQL tool before the orchestrator's rule change; none after.

findings.title: Search-owned '{City} homes for sale' duplicated onto every place page; gate rewritten to enforce the duplication
findings.claim: Since commit ffcc52e80 (2026-09-17, 'Node: none'), /cities/{city} and /homes-for-sale/{city} carry the identical title and H1 '{City} homes for sale' (live: Bend), and the same phrase is the H1 on neighborhood, zip, subdivision and oregon pages, so the site's strongest place pages and its search pages now compete for the same head query. scripts/check-seo-shell.mjs was changed in the same commit to REQUIRE this, so the documented fix (city -> '{City} real estate', PAGE_OUTLINE.md:64-66,226-228) now fails CI.
findings.evidence: Live 2026-09-22: /cities/bend title 'Bend homes for sale | Ryan Realty, Central Oregon' H1 'Bend homes for sale' index,follow; /homes-for-sale/bend same title, same H1, index,follow; both in core.xml. git show --stat ffcc52e80: 27 files incl. app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx, app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx, app/zip/[zip]/page.tsx, app/subdivisions/[slug]/page.tsx, app/oregon/[city]/page.tsx, scripts/check-seo-shell.mjs (+22/-22). check-seo-shell.mjs:102-107 'city H1 must be "{city} homes for sale"', 129-130 neighborhood H1 must carry it. PAGE_OUTLINE.md:53 'Change H1. Search owns that phrase.'; SITE_PAGES_E2E.md:9 'Search owns {City} homes for sale. City guide owns {City} real estate.'
findings.why_it_matters: One query, two identical indexable pages: Google picks one (often the thinner search page) and the other loses; the same pattern is now stamped on every place class, so the whole place tree is competing with the search tree instead of covering distinct queries ('Bend real estate', 'Awbrey Butte neighborhood', '97702 homes'). This landed five days before the audit and outside the work graph.
findings.proposed_fix: Restore the one-URL-per-query lock: city page title/H1 '{City} real estate' (or '{City}, Oregon real estate and neighborhoods'), neighborhood '{Neighborhood} neighborhood, Bend' style, plat '{Plat} subdivision, {City}', keep '{Place} homes for sale' only on /homes-for-sale/*. Revert check-seo-shell.mjs lines 97-107 and 129-130 to assert the lock (search-only phrase) instead of the duplication, add a test that no two sitemapped URL classes share a title template, and record the ruling in PAGE_OUTLINE.md.

findings.title: About 59% of the 1,815 sitemapped subdivision browse URLs are indexable empty search pages
findings.claim: The sitemap emits /homes-for-sale/{city}/{sub} for every Central Oregon (city, MLS subdivision name) pair with >=3 lifetime listings regardless of current inventory; only 782 of the 1,919 qualifying pairs have an active listing, so roughly 1,100 sitemapped, index,follow pages render 'No homes match this search right now' under an H1 promising homes for sale, many with MLS-abbreviation names (clal, canyonv, cascade-view-allotmt).
findings.evidence: app/sitemap.ts:417-429 (SUBDIVISION_SITEMAP_MIN_LIFETIME_LISTINGS = 3, all statuses). db-exposure.mjs: subdivision_city_inventory_mv 6,888 rows -> CO pairs 2,218, >=3 lifetime 1,919, with >=1 active 782. Live sample (every 151st browse URL in geo.xml, 12 URLs): 9 render 'No homes match this search right now' with <meta name=robots content='index, follow'> and 0 listing links (bp-*.html). Contrast: the matrix leg already noindexes verified-zero combos (search-metadata.ts:63-70, W3.1/W3.2) but the 2-segment browse page does not.
findings.why_it_matters: Over a thousand submitted pages whose only content is an empty-result message is the textbook programmatic-thin-content signal; it spends crawl budget, depresses the quality assessment of the whole /homes-for-sale/ path, and gives AI engines nothing to quote. The comment in sitemap.ts argues sold history is the page's value, but the browse page shows no sold history when empty.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply the existing verified-zero rule to the 2-segment browse page: when the pair has 0 active AND 0 pending, render noindex,follow and omit from the sitemap (fail-open on unknown, as W3.1 does). Where a plat page exists for the same slug (651 cases), canonical/301 the browse URL to /subdivisions/{slug} instead. Reject MLS-abbreviation names as page names (require a display name from the registry or the recorded plat label).

findings.title: 2,643 plat pages are sitemap-only orphans since SITE-128 removed their city-page links (2026-09-18)
findings.claim: The home page, the city pages, /site-index and the community pages link to zero /subdivisions/{slug} URLs; the /subdivisions index links 59 registry plats. Commit fc68066dc (SITE-128) deleted the 'Subdivisions in {city}' section with a comment that 'A–Z /subdivisions is the directory', but no A–Z directory exists, so most of the 2,643 plat pages in geo.xml are reachable only through the sitemap and the listing pages of plats that currently have inventory.
findings.evidence: Anchor counts from raw HTML: / 0 plat links of 303; /cities/bend 0 of 995; /site-index 0 of 313; /communities/tetherow 0; /subdivisions 59 of 226 (app/subdivisions/page.tsx:63 registryChildPlats()). git show fc68066dc -- app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx: '-heading={`Subdivisions in ${cityName}`}'; app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx:434-440 comment. Remaining inbound: app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx:865 platHref, and <=24 sister links per plat (PLAT_SISTER_CAP).
findings.why_it_matters: Pages with no internal links get little PageRank and are crawled and indexed reluctantly; a 2,600-page long tail that only the sitemap knows about cannot be the moat Matt describes. The removal happened four days ago as a 'look' change and nothing measured the link loss.
findings.proposed_fix: Build the directory the comment promises: /subdivisions/{city} A–Z pages (HTML lists, <=200 links each, paginated by letter), linked from each city page's child-places section (name-only cards are fine) and from /subdivisions; communities link their child plats; keep the plat -> city/community/neighborhood back-links. Add a gate that every sitemapped URL class has >=1 inbound HTML link from a non-sitemap page (crawl the built site or the route map).

findings.title: Two indexable URL families per subdivision (651 overlaps) with the same H1
findings.claim: A subdivision can be served as /subdivisions/{plat-slug} (GIS polygon, sold history) and as /homes-for-sale/{city}/{mls-name} (MLS name match); 651 slugs are in the sitemap under both, both index,follow, both headed '{Name} homes for sale', and they can disagree (the browse twin of Deschutes River Woods says no homes match while the plat twin lists 20).
findings.evidence: comm -12 of browse slugs (1,723) and plat slugs (2,642) from geo.xml = 651. Live: /homes-for-sale/bend/deschutes-river-woods index, H1 'Deschutes River Woods homes for sale', 'No homes match this search right now'; /subdivisions/deschutes-river-woods index, same H1, 20 listing links. subdivision_plat_closed_mv: deschutes-river-woods closed_by_name 0, closed_in_polygon 3,018 (the MLS never files that name).
findings.why_it_matters: Duplicate entities split ranking signals and confuse both Google and answer engines about which page is the subdivision; the split is structural (name vs polygon) so it recurs for every plat.
findings.proposed_fix: One canonical per subdivision: when a plat polygon exists, the plat page is canonical and the browse URL 301s (or canonicals) to it, with the plat page absorbing the MLS-name inventory list; when no polygon exists, the browse page stands alone and is indexable only with active inventory. PAGE_OUTLINE.md:53 already states this rule for communities/neighborhoods ('301 to the place URL'); extend it to plats and gate it.

findings.title: Sitemap submits 105 /zip URLs that return 404
findings.claim: app/sitemap.ts emits /zip/{zip} for every PostalCode with an active listing statewide (115 URLs, including Klamath Falls, Ashland, Medford, Portland ZIPs), but app/zip/[zip] is dynamicParams=false over the 10 CANONICAL_ZIPS, so 105 submitted URLs 404.
findings.evidence: app/sitemap.ts:515-539 (no region or canonical filter); app/zip/[zip]/page.tsx:170 dynamicParams=false, :173 generateStaticParams over CANONICAL_ZIPS; zip-constants.ts:67 lists 10; comm of sitemap zips vs canonical = 10 overlap, 105 sitemap-only; live /zip/97501 and /zip/97219 -> 404 'Page not found'.
findings.why_it_matters: 404s in a sitemap are a direct crawl-quality signal against the domain and waste the budget the plat pages need; Search Console will report them as errors on every crawl.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit only CANONICAL_ZIPS in the sitemap (import the same set the route uses); add a sitemap contract test that every emitted /zip URL resolves in generateStaticParams.

findings.title: Property-type pages: indexable, unsitemapped, unlinked from nav, and twinned with sitemapped presets
findings.claim: The 260 place-type pages (7 cities x 10 types, 19 communities x 10 types) are index,follow with strong count-bearing titles, yet none is in any sitemap or in the header/footer; city pages link their 10, community pages link none of theirs. For every (city, type) a second indexable page exists at /homes-for-sale/{city}/{preset} (sitemapped) with a near-identical query target.
findings.evidence: grep -c '/types/' urls-all.txt = 0; lib/site-nav.ts has no type links; live /cities/bend/types/single-family '757 single-family homes for sale in Bend, Oregon' index vs /homes-for-sale/bend/single-family 'Single-Family Homes in Bend' index (matrix.xml); /cities/bend/types/condos vs /homes-for-sale/bend/condos; /communities/tetherow: 0 anchors to /communities/tetherow/types/*; grep 'types/' app/communities/[slug]/** = none.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Bend condos for sale' and 'Tetherow single family homes' are exactly the property-type queries Matt expects to own; today the intent is split across two URLs, the richer one is invisible to the crawler and the menu, and the community variants are orphans.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one URL per (place, type): keep the place-type page (count, band, map, rail) as canonical, make the preset twin canonical to it (or 301), sitemap the winners, add a Property types column to the mega-menu (MASTER_SPEC §4.3 already specifies one) and a types row on every community page.

findings.title: Indexable plat pages with no recent sales render templated filler at scale; one sitemapped plat 500s
findings.claim: The plat index bar is 10 lifetime closed sales with no recency or inventory condition, so 454 of the 2,642 indexable plats have had no sale in two years and pages like bartel-addition (10 sales, last 2020, zero active) publish ~22 template sentences with the name and one number swapped. /subdivisions/blakley-heights (1,234 closes, in geo.xml) returns HTTP 500.
findings.evidence: subdivision-index.ts:48 (=10); db-exposure.mjs: 454 indexable plats with last_close_date < 2024-09-22; subs/bartel-addition.html text ('2 homes closed in Bartel Addition in 2020', 'Bartel Addition has had fewer sales we can attribute to it on its own than a fair buyer's or seller's verdict needs'); txt-bartel ∩ txt-carriage = 4 identical lines of 22; curl /subdivisions/blakley-heights -> 500 twice.
findings.why_it_matters: Hundreds of near-identical, data-free pages are what Google's helpful-content and scaled-content systems demote site-wide, taking the strong plats (Tetherow Phase 1, DRW) down with them; a 500 on a submitted URL is a crawl error.
findings.proposed_fix: Index a plat only when it has a polygon AND (>=1 active or pending listing OR >=1 closed sale in the last 36 months OR >=25 lifetime closes); everything else stays reachable as noindex,follow. Fix the blakley-heights 500 (reproduce locally; likely a section read throwing under maxDuration 60) and add a nightly HEAD sweep of sitemap URLs that alerts on any 5xx.

findings.title: No unique prose exists for any plat or browse page (subdivision_descriptions is empty)
findings.claim: subdivision_descriptions holds 0 rows; every one of the 2,643 plat pages and 1,815 browse pages is generated from the same sentence templates plus numbers, so nothing on them is quotable by an answer engine or distinguishable by Google beyond the figures.
findings.evidence: Two query shapes on subdivision_descriptions returned []; app/actions/subdivision-descriptions.ts:40-53 falls back to getSubdivisionBlurb; generators at :57-110 exist but never populated the table; sample plat text in notes §3.
findings.why_it_matters: Depth that Google and AI models can see is sentences with facts, dates and sources; templates at 4,000-page scale are the opposite signal. This is the gap between 'so much information to expose' and what is exposed.
findings.proposed_fix: Author real prose for the pages that clear the index bar, in tiers: hand-written for the 13 districts, 19 communities and the ~100 plats with the most closes; LLM-drafted from verified fields (plat recording, streets, schools, sold-by-year) with a human review stamp for the rest; store in subdivision_descriptions with a source line and a reviewed_at; the page renders nothing generic when the row is missing.

findings.title: 61 out-of-area /oregon pages are indexed as 'outside our market' after the cap was widened 25 -> 100
findings.claim: Portland, Salem, Eugene, Albany, Medford and 56 other out-of-area cities have indexable pages titled 'N {City} homes for sale, outside our market', emitted to geo.xml, because OUT_OF_AREA_INDEXABLE_TOP_N was raised from 25 to 100; the IA doc classifies /oregon/[city] as refer-out.
findings.evidence: grep '^/oregon/' urls-geo.txt = 61; live /oregon/portland and /oregon/medford index,follow; lib/out-of-area-cities.ts:46-52 ('WIDENED 25 -> 100'); docs/plans/PUBLIC_PRODUCT/SITE_PAGES.md:83 'Out of area | /oregon/[city] | Refer-out.'
findings.why_it_matters: A Bend brokerage ranking pages that say 'outside our market' for Portland dilutes the Central Oregon entity Google and AI engines should associate with the domain, and any traffic they earn cannot convert to a listing appointment.
findings.proposed_fix: Matt decides: either noindex,follow every /oregon page (keep as referral landing for existing inbound) or keep a small set with a documented referral partner; remove the rest from the sitemap. Record the number in lib/out-of-area-cities.ts with the ruling.

findings.title: Sitemap and nav carry redirect sources and duplicates
findings.claim: core.xml lists /luxury-homes-bend, which 308s to a query URL that the site itself noindexes (minPrice is a blocked key), and the header/footer link it 3 times; geo.xml lists /homes-for-sale/bend/awbrey-butte, which 301s to the neighborhood page; 30 URLs appear twice across children.
findings.evidence: curl /luxury-homes-bend -> 308 https://ryan-realty.com/homes-for-sale/bend?minPrice=1500000; next.config.ts:434; lib/seo-routing.ts:33-35; app/sitemap.ts:101; lib/site-nav.ts:181,271; curl /homes-for-sale/bend/awbrey-butte -> 301 /cities/bend/awbrey-butte; sort urls-all.txt | uniq -d = 30.
findings.why_it_matters: A submitted redirect and a nav link into a noindexed URL leak link equity and produce 'redirect' and 'submitted but noindex' rows in Search Console; small but self-inflicted.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop redirect sources from the sitemap (assert every emitted URL is a 200 self-canonical in lib/sitemap.contract.test.ts), point the 'Luxury homes' door at an indexable page (/homes-for-sale/bend/luxury is already in matrix.xml), dedupe the static seed vs dynamic city loop, and skip browse slugs that collide with neighborhood slugs.

findings.title: Header exposes neither property types nor neighborhoods, and its Buy doors are ?view= URLs
findings.claim: The live header/mega-menu offers cities and resort communities only; no property-type or neighborhood destinations exist in it despite MASTER_SPEC §4.3 specifying Cities / Featured Neighborhoods / Property Types columns, and the primary Buy links are /homes-for-sale?view=map and ?view=list (10 anchors on the home page to non-canonical query URLs).
findings.evidence: lib/site-nav.ts:105-241 (KB_TOP_NAV/KB_MENU_GROUPS), lib/site/chrome-mega.ts columns Cities/Communities/Browse; grep 'href="/homes-for-sale' live-home.html: 7x ?view=list, 3x ?view=map; docs/MASTER_SPEC.md:1706-1707; PAGE_OUTLINE.md:67 notes the index route still self-canonicals ?view.
findings.why_it_matters: The menu is the crawl path a human and a crawler both use; if the depth Matt built (13 districts, 260 type pages, 2,600 plats) is not in it, neither users nor Googlebot discover it from the home page, and the top nav's strongest links go to a URL variant Google should not index.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement the spec'd mega-menu: Buy -> canonical /homes-for-sale plus Property types (10 for Bend), Areas -> Cities, Bend neighborhoods (13), Communities, Subdivisions A–Z; footer-by-city with the same children. Strip ?view= from nav hrefs (view is a client preference).

findings.title: geo.xml lastmod is now() on 4,740 of 4,827 URLs
findings.claim: Every place leg stamps lastModified: now, so the sitemap tells Google that 4,740 pages changed today, every day; Google documents that it ignores lastmod when it is not accurate.
findings.evidence: grep '<lastmod>' sitemap-geo.xml | cut -c1-10 | sort | uniq -c -> 4740 2026-09-22; app/sitemap.ts:346,426,443,462,534 `lastModified: now`.
findings.why_it_matters: Accurate lastmod is the cheapest way to get a 9,000-URL site recrawled where it changed (a new listing in a plat) instead of everywhere; today it is noise.
findings.proposed_fix: Use real change dates: plat pages -> last_close_date or last listing modified in the polygon (subdivision_plat_closed_mv / listing_tile_mv), browse pages -> newest listing modified_at, city/community -> geo_snapshot_mv.refreshed_at; keep now() only for truly daily pages.

findings.title: Place pages ship 1.7 to 3.8 MB of HTML
findings.claim: /cities/bend is 3.77 MB of HTML, /cities/bend/awbrey-butte 2.0 MB, /cities/bend/types/single-family 1.68 MB, /communities/tetherow 0.92 MB, a listing page 0.95 MB, because basemap street and polygon data is server-rendered into the document.
findings.evidence: curl size_download in the probe logs; next.config.ts:499-500 outputFileTracingIncludes data/basemap/streets/*.json for community and subdivision pages; the listing page HTML contains hundreds of street-name <title> elements.
findings.why_it_matters: Multi-megabyte documents raise TTFB/LCP on mobile and cost crawl budget per fetch; Googlebot also truncates very large responses. It is not the ranking cause but it is a drag on every place page.
findings.proposed_fix: Move basemap streets/water and polygon rings out of the SSR payload into a cached JSON fetch (or static files) loaded by the atlas client; keep only the facts and links in HTML. Measure HTML size in the route parity/taste receipts.

findings.title: Only 13 neighborhood pages exist and all are Bend; other cities have no neighborhood layer
findings.claim: The neighborhoods table has 13 rows (Bend's GIS districts); Redmond, Sisters, Sunriver, La Pine, Prineville and Madras have no neighborhood pages, so their only children are MLS-name browse pages and plats, and MASTER_SPEC's 'Neighborhoods' mega-menu 'Other areas (Redmond, Sisters, Sunriver)' has nothing to point at.
findings.evidence: Row read of neighborhoods joined to cities: 13 rows, all city_slug=bend; boundaries geo_type=neighborhood: 14 Bend districts + resort slugs only; docs/MASTER_SPEC.md:1707.
findings.why_it_matters: The 13 Bend district pages are the site's best-built place pages (1,300-char prose, polygon, hero); the same shape for Redmond's areas (Dry Canyon, Eagle Crest, NW Redmond) is the missing middle between city and plat for six cities.
findings.proposed_fix: Define 4-8 named areas per non-Bend city from existing polygons or plat clusters, add rows to neighborhoods with prose and boundary_source, and let the existing route and sitemap leg pick them up.
